instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a few changes of water until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 1 3/4 cups water, bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered while the salmon cooks.

Heat the oven to 400°F. In a small bowl, whisk the 3 tbsp gochujang with the 2 minced garlic cloves, the juice of half the lime, the honey, sesame oil, soy sauce and rice vinegar until smooth. Spoon 2 tbsp of the glaze into a separate small bowl and keep it for the end.
Pat the salmon dry with paper towels and sprinkle both sides with the salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over high heat. Put the salmon in skin side down and cook for 3 minutes, brushing the top of each fillet with the glaze from the big bowl as it sears.

Move the skillet to the oven and roast for 8 to 10 minutes. That should be about 130°F at the thickest part if you have a thermometer. Without one, press the thickest part with a fork: it should flake but still look a little glossy in the center.
Let the salmon rest in the pan for 5 minutes. Thinly slice 2 green onions.
Taste a corner of the salmon. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze from the other half of the lime.
Spoon the saved glaze over the salmon and sprinkle with the sesame seeds and green onions. Serve over the rice.
method_notes: The sauce is the same in every version read: gochujang, honey, garlic, sesame oil, soy and an acid, brushed on and roasted at 400°F or broiled. The Crumby Kitchen sears the skin side first and finishes in the oven with lime in the glaze; Food Network UK broils with mirin and sugar and no garlic; Cooking Therapy bakes at 425°F then broils. This follows The Crumby Kitchen, with a little of the glaze saved clean for the end and rice added to make it a dinner. Start the rice first to stay near 30 minutes.
